[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 10, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 10 at 7375 Lindell Road, Las Vegas, NV. Both datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap independently give this same address, and both datacenterMap and a second directory (Baxtel) independently agree on 40 MW of capacity and 350,000 sq ft for this building. Two independent aggregator directories agree on 40 MW and 350,000 sq ft for this building, aggregator-sourced leads-only data, not confirmed by the operator, so not applied to critical_it_mw. Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading:
Switch is a private data center operator headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada. DigitalBridge Investment Management and IFM Investors announced a take-private acquisition of Switch in May 2022 for approximately $11 billion, completed later that year, after which Switch ceased to be an independent SEC filer.

The company's own site describes more than 26 years of operations and names five exascale campus locations, Tahoe Reno, Las Vegas, Atlanta, Grand Rapids, and Austin/Houston, without stating a precise founding year, founder, or current aggregate capacity figure beyond a general claim of modular power density up to gigawatt scale per facility. Switch's Tahoe Reno and Las Vegas campuses in Nevada are among the industry's largest known single-site data center developments, though no square footage or megawatt total for either was located on the operator's site this session.

The registry here tracks 15 Switch facilities across three states, Georgia, Nevada, and Texas, a subset of the five campus markets named on the operator's own site, which additionally lists Michigan (Grand Rapids). No dollar-denominated construction investment figure specific to these states was located this session.
